title: Datacenter Systems Spending To Go Through The Roof In 2027
gist: Gartner's November 2026 forecast, which now breaks out IaaS, shows datacenter systems plus IaaS spending reaching $1.73 trillion in 2027 (+48%), overtaking enterprise software ($1.68T, +14.7%) for the first time, with datacenter systems growth cooling from 73.8% in 2026 to 55.4% in 2027. Timothy Prickett Morgan notes core IT growth is running ~7–8X GDP, estimates about half of 2026 systems spending growth is price inflation from scarcity, and warns 2027 may be the peak amid political and power-supply backlash.

insights.claim: Gartner's forecast has combined datacenter systems plus IaaS spending surpassing enterprise software in 2027, at $1.73 trillion (up 48 percent) versus $1.68 trillion for enterprise software (up 14.7 percent), reversing a long history in which software revenues were 2X to 3X systems sales.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Hardware/IaaS is now the largest core IT bucket — capex beneficiaries (servers, networking, storage, cloud) out-growing software.
insights.quote: $1.73 trillion for the hardware spending, up 48 percent year on year, compared to $1.68 trillion for enterprise software

insights.claim: Gartner expects datacenter systems spending growth to cool to 55.4 percent in 2027 after an explosive 73.8 percent in 2026.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Growth deceleration from extreme levels — second-derivative risk for hardware stocks even as absolute spend rises.
insights.locator: But as you can also plainly see, Gartner thinks

insights.claim: Gartner's November 2026 forecast newly separates Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) from the IT services segment, allowing systems sales and capacity rentals to be viewed together.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Better visibility into cloud infrastructure rental spend versus labor-based IT services.
insights.locator: One new twist has been added

insights.claim: IT services spending excluding IaaS is forecast to grow a more anemic 4.9 percent in 2027, still almost 2X global GDP growth.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Services firms lag the AI hardware boom; growth near mature-market norms.
insights.locator: The other neat bit is that spending on IT services

insights.claim: Prickett Morgan's rule of thumb from decades of tracking is that mature IT markets grow at around 2X GDP, but core IT spending growth is running about 8X GDP in 2026 and 7.3X in 2027 if Gartner and World Bank forecasts hold.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The current gap to GDP is ~4x the historical norm — a sign of boom conditions and of mean-reversion risk.
insights.quote: We are not living in normal times, clearly.
insights.locator: The world has changed so much

insights.claim: Core IT (systems, enterprise software and services) was a little more than a third of overall IT spending in 2012 and will exceed two thirds by the end of 2027.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Spending mix has shifted structurally toward enterprise infrastructure and away from devices/telecom.
insights.locator: The world has changed so much

insights.claim: Datacenter systems revenues grew an average of just 2.3 percent annually from 2013 to 2021, below average global GDP growth of 2.7 percent, so the systems market was 'beyond mature' until the pandemic and GenAI.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Underscores how abnormal the current hardware cycle is relative to its base rate.
insights.locator: The average growth rate for datacenter systems revenues

insights.claim: Despite talk of 'Softwaremageddon', enterprise software spending has been on a steeper growth line since around 2017, though it is not steepening the way datacenter systems spending is.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Pushes back on AI-kills-software narratives — software spend continues healthy, if slower, growth.
insights.locator: That’s systems, enterprise software, and services

insights.claim: Prickett Morgan estimates roughly half of 2026 datacenter systems spending growth reflects supply-demand driven price inflation and half reflects actual increases in delivered capacity, explicitly calling it an educated guess.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: If half of growth is price, real capacity growth is far lower than headline spend — margins for scarce components (GPUs, memory) are elevated and vulnerable when supply catches up.
insights.quote: But that is just an educated guess.
insights.locator: Now, this chart is just expressing currency inflation

insights.claim: Companies are becoming less stingy with hardware budgets because they cannot afford to miss the GenAI wave, a dynamic resembling the Dot Com boom, except that hyperscalers and cloud builders already exist and hog GPU and XPU allocations.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Bubble analogy plus allocation concentration: hyperscalers capture supply, enterprises compete for scraps.
insights.quote: In this regard, the GenAI boom most definitely resembles the Dot Com boom.
insights.locator: Core IT spending was not driven by servers

insights.claim: Several forecasters think 2027 will be the peak for IT spending, not for lack of demand but due to a political uprising against tech titans and their datacenter and electricity needs, combined with doubts that power generation and distribution can scale to meet datacenter demand.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Power constraints and political backlash are the key cap on the AI capex cycle — watch post-2027 forecasts and power/grid policy.
insights.quote: There are more than a few prognosticators who think that next year will be the peak

insights.claim: The datacenter business had a rough couple of days after last week's US elections, though the author expects optimism to continue 'right up to the moment when it might not'.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Election outcome is a near-term sentiment risk for datacenter equities.
insights.quote: Right up to the moment when it might not.
insights.locator: It was a rough couple of days

insights.claim: Forecasting beyond 12 to 18 months is unreliable given wobbly near-term data, so 2028 outcomes remain highly uncertain.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Discount long-dated capex forecasts; focus on 12-18 month visibility.
insights.locator: There is a lot that can and cannot happen in 2028
